title: Optimistic UI: Making Interfaces Feel Instant
summary: This lesson explains Optimistic UI, a technique where the interface updates immediately after a user action without waiting for server confirmation. It highlights the 400ms threshold for perceived latency and defines when to use this pattern versus showing a loading state.

transcript.text: Click like. One waits, one feels instant.
The slow one waits for the server before anything moves.
The fast one updates the screen first, then syncs in the background.
Same network. One just stopped waiting.
Your brain reads anything under 400 milliseconds as instant.
Past that, a spinner reads as broken, even when it works fine.
You're not buying speed, you're buying the feeling of it.
So what if the request fails?
The fast one rolls back. The like undoes itself, the count returns to where it was.
Optimistic isn't ignoring errors, it's betting on success.
This is Optimistic UI. You assume the happy path, render now, and reconcile when the server replies.
99% of the time, it was right anyway.
But not everywhere. Never fake a payment, a transfer, or anything you can't undo.
Show those the truth, even if the truth is a spinner.
Follow for more UX patterns. Save this for your next build.

on_screen_text: Bet on success. Handle the rare miss.
before_after: Transition from a 'Wait for Server' model (slow, visible delay) to an 'Update First, Sync After' model (instant feel).
